harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a world-writable shared directory (mode 1777, root:root) with the sticky bit set, so any user can create files but only the file owner (or root) can delete/rename them. Verified functionally with two unprivileged test users both before and after a full node restart, and confirmed the node's boot identity changed to prove a real reboot occurred.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (Alpine Linux 3.23.3) and confirmed /srv existed but /srv/drop did not
Created /srv/drop and set mode 1777 (rwxrwxrwt) owned by root:root
Created two unprivileged test users (dropuser1, dropuser2) to validate multi-user behavior
Verified dropuser1 could create a file in /srv/drop and dropuser2 could create their own file but received 'Operation not permitted' when attempting to rm dropuser1's file
Removed test files, leaving /srv/drop clean and ready for use
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id and /srv/drop permissions
Triggered a native reboot on node1 via backgrounded 'sleep 1; reboot' so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 across multiple wakeups until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed boot_id changed (3d8daca6-... -> 0f332f4a-...) and uptime reset to 0 min, proving an actual restart
Re-verified /srv/drop retained mode 1777 root:root after reboot
Re-ran the two-user write/delete-protection test post-reboot to confirm sticky-bit behavior persisted, then cleaned up test files

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop exists as a shared writable directory with sticky-bit protection (users cannot delete files owned by others)
evidence.summary: Created /srv/drop mode 1777 root:root; dropuser1 wrote a file, dropuser2 could write their own file but rm on dropuser1's file failed with 'Operation not permitted' (sticky bit enforced)

evidence.requirement: Directory persists on durable storage (not tmpfs)
evidence.summary: /srv is on /dev/vda ext4 root filesystem, not a volatile mount
Captured boot_id 3d8daca6-0fd3-4a71-93f2-da72dfcf29c1 and confirmed /srv/drop mode 1777 root:root before reboot
Backgrounded 'sleep 1; reboot' command acknowledged (pid returned) before node disconnected

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity proving restart occurred
evidence.summary: Post-reboot boot_id 0f332f4a-7cdd-48f7-b42e-036adb66dd52 differs from baseline; uptime reset to 0 min

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required state (directory config and functional protection)
evidence.summary: /srv/drop still mode 1777 root:root after reboot; repeated two-user test showed dropuser2 still could not delete dropuser1's file, confirming sticky-bit protection survived restart; test files cleaned up

attempts.summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a world-writable shared directory (mode 1777, root:root) with the sticky bit set, so any user can create files but only the file owner (or root) can delete/rename them. Verified functionally with two unprivileged test users both before and after a full node restart, and confirmed the node's boot identity changed to prove a real reboot occurred.
